B2-1-0.name: Feed the verb
B2-1-0.prompt: Completa cada verbo con un gerundio sobre tu propia familia y luego di la misma idea después de una preposición.
answers: I can’t stand being interrupted at dinner. / I’m tired of being interrupted at dinner.
My brother keeps borrowing my clothes. / He never apologises for borrowing my clothes.
We’ve given up arguing about politics. / We’re tired of arguing about politics.
I’m good at calming everyone down. / My family relies on me for calming everyone down.
Nobody here objects to sharing the cooking. / Everybody is happy about sharing the cooking.

B2-1-1.name: Frame it first
B2-1-1.prompt: Di cada idea dos veces: primero como una frase simple y luego reformulada con una cláusula nominal después de “be”.
items: they still argue about the house
answers: Nobody apologised. / The problem is that nobody apologised.
My sister moved abroad. / The truth is that my sister moved abroad.
We only meet at weddings. / The sad thing is that we only meet at weddings.
He forgot my birthday. / What hurt me was that he forgot my birthday.
They still argue about the house. / The issue is that they still argue about the house.

B2-2-0.name: Did it happen?
B2-2-0.prompt: Para cada indicación, di la frase y luego explica si la acción se realizó o no.
items: hand in the form / obligatory, done
bring a gift / brought one unnecessarily
tell the manager / not done, regretted
answers: We had to hand in the form. (It was obligatory, and we did.)
We didn’t have to pay the deposit. (It wasn’t required, so we didn’t pay it.)
I needn’t have brought a gift. (I brought one, but it wasn’t necessary.)
I should have told the manager. (I didn’t, and I regret it.)
She was supposed to lock the door. (She was expected to, but she forgot.)

B2-2-1.name: Three levels of certainty
B2-2-1.prompt: Para cada pista, da tres explicaciones: una casi segura, una posible y una que puedes descartar.
items: his coat is still on the chair
all the lights are on at midnight
her phone goes straight to voicemail
the window is open from the inside
answers: He must have left in a hurry. / He might have gone to a meeting. / He can’t have gone home without his coat.
Someone must have been hungry. / The kids might have eaten it. / It can’t have been the dog — it can’t reach the table.
Someone must have forgotten to turn them off. / They might have had a party. / They can’t have been asleep.
Her battery must have died. / She might have switched it off. / She can’t have blocked me — we spoke an hour ago.
Someone inside must have opened it. / It might have been the cleaner. / It can’t have been a burglar from outside.

B2-3-0.name: Commas or no commas
B2-3-0.prompt: Une cada par en una sola frase y di si la cláusula necesita comas y por qué.
items: I visited Porto. It sits on a river.
The street was too steep. We stayed on it.
My cousin lives in Cali. He never leaves.
That’s the museum. It opened last year.
This is the year. Everything changed then.
answers: I visited Porto, which sits on a river. (Commas: Porto is already identified; this is extra information.)
The street (that) we stayed on was too steep. (No commas: the clause tells us which street.)
My cousin, who lives in Cali, never leaves. (Commas if I have one cousin; the clause is extra information.)
That’s the museum that opened last year. (No commas: the clause identifies which museum.)
This is the year when everything changed. (No commas: the clause identifies which year.)

B2-3-1.name: Stack three, stack four
B2-3-1.prompt: Describe cada cosa con tres adjetivos en el orden correcto y luego agrega un cuarto sin romper el orden.
answers: a tall old brick building → a tall old red brick building
a small bright square room → a small bright square white room
a colourful little wooden stall → a colourful little old wooden stall
a beautiful long stone bridge → a beautiful long old stone bridge
a cosy small traditional café → a cosy small old traditional Colombian café

B2-3-2.name: Same contrast, three ways
B2-3-2.prompt: Expresa cada contraste tres veces: con despite, con although y con however.
items: far from the centre / well connected
answers: Despite the price, it’s worth it. / Although it’s expensive, it’s worth it. / It’s expensive. However, it’s worth it.
Despite the noise, it’s lively. / Although it’s noisy, it’s lively. / It’s noisy. However, it’s lively.
Despite being far from the centre, it’s well connected. / Although it’s far from the centre, it’s well connected. / It’s far from the centre. However, it’s well connected.
Despite its size, it’s never boring. / Although it’s small, it’s never boring. / It’s small. However, it’s never boring.
Despite the rain, it’s beautiful. / Although it’s rainy, it’s beautiful. / It’s rainy. However, it’s beautiful.
